claim: Best real test accuracy is not significant against the shuffled-label null
test: share of 200 null runs >= best Task 4 test accuracy

claim: Genome-grouped CV gives 45-55 % on every representation
test: cv_leave_group_out_balanced.csv, all 18 rep x model rows

claim: Pair-sign agreement ~chance, unseen-pair Spearman ~0, GC removal changes nothing, LOGO near chance
test: these numbers were given in the prompt

claim: "AT-rich pathogens such as H. pylori, S. aureus and Listeria in the training set" drive the AT-rich weights
result: Helicobacter: test, Staphylococcus: train, Listeria: test

claim: Strongest k-mers are most enriched in specific named training genomes (GCGC/CGCG: P. aeruginosa, M. tb; GGGC/CCGT/ACGG: S. coelicolor; TAAA/TTTA/TTTTAA: S. aureus)
test: rank 18 training genomes by mean frequency of each word; claim holds if a named genome is in the top 2
result: 8/8 words. GCGC: top=P.aerugi,S.coelic; CGCG: top=S.coelic,P.aerugi; GGGC: top=S.coelic,P.putida; CCGT: top=S.coelic,B.longum; ACGG: top=S.coelic,B.longum; TAAA: top=S.aureus,B.anthra; TTTA: top=S.aureus,B.anthra; TTTTAA: top2=['Staphylococcus aureus', 'Bacillus anthracis']

claim: Dropping any one training genome substantially changes the top-20 k=4 coefficient list (overlap well under 50 %)
test: refit k=4 BoW LogReg 18 times, each without one training genome; overlap of top-20 |coef| words
result: overlap median 70%, min 55% (dropping Bacillus subtilis 168), max 85%

claim: Within each test genome >=80 % of fragments get the same label; genome-level accuracy about 3/6
test: k=4 BoW LogReg trained on 18 genomes; share of majority call within each of 6 test genomes; genome vote
result: majority share per genome 89%, 54%, 68%, 78%, 79%, 74%; genome vote 4/6

claim: For most (paired-genus) fragments the nearest neighbour from another genome is the genus partner, which explains below-chance label purity
test: 4-mer standardized space; 1200 fragments from the 12 paired genomes; first neighbour not from own genome
result: neighbour is genus partner 43% (chance 1/23 = 4 %); label agreement 28%

claim: Genome-identity errors go to genomes of the same genus or similar GC, not to random genomes
test: 18-way genome-ID LogReg (5-fold random split); |genome GC difference| between true and predicted genome for errors vs random wrong genome
result: error rate 19%; median |dGC| errors 1.7 pts vs random 11.7 pts; errors into genus partner 41% (random ~24% for paired genomes)

claim: CTAG obs/exp (2nd-order Markov) < 0.5 in most genomes, and no pathogen vs non-pathogen difference
test: genome-mean frequencies; ratio f(CTAG)f(TA)/(f(CTA)f(TAG)); Mann-Whitney, 12 vs 12 genomes
result: 7/24 genomes below 0.5 (median 0.84, range 0.19-1.15); class medians 0.80 vs 0.87, p=0.58

claim: Restriction palindromes (CAGCTG, GAGCTC, CTTAAG, CGCG) vary more between genera than inside a matched pair, and do not separate the labels
test: Markov obs/exp per genome; mean |difference| within the 6 pairs vs between genomes of different genera; Mann-Whitney by label
result: CAGCTG: within 0.13 vs between 0.30, label p=0.71; GAGCTC: within 0.13 vs between 0.32, label p=0.47; CTTAAG: within 0.18 vs between 0.24, label p=0.58; CGCG: within 0.03 vs between 0.16, label p=0.16

claim: A word and its reverse complement can get different coefficients; counting canonical k-mers will not change test accuracy
test: k=4 BoW LogReg: Spearman of coef(w) vs coef(revcomp w) over 120 pairs; refit on 136 canonical 4-mers
result: Spearman 0.66, opposite sign in 23% of pairs; test acc 256-dim 0.579 vs canonical 0.578

claim: Pathogens sit at both ends of the GC range, so one linear GC term fails
test: genome GC distance from the median GC, pathogens vs non-pathogens (one-sided Mann-Whitney)
result: pathogen GC 0.33-0.67, non-pathogen 0.35-0.72; median |GC-median| 0.090 vs 0.094, p=0.62

claim: Pathogen-only DNA (e.g. O157:H7 sequence absent from K-12) is a small minority of fragments, has unusual GC, and is where any pathogen signal would be
test: E. coli O157:H7 fragments: share of 16-mers present anywhere in K-12 (both strands); <10 % shared = pathogen-specific. Compare |GC - genome mean| and leave-one-genus-out P(pathogen) of the k=4 model. Other pairs are different species (near-zero exact sharing) and only reported in the detail file
result: O157-specific fragments 18% (Listeria pair 33%; different-species pairs 75-100 %); |GC dev| specific 6.4 vs shared 3.7 pts; P(pathogen) specific 0.62 vs shared 0.78
